field_excerpts: A motile cilium where the axoneme has a ring of nine outer microtubule doublets plus two central microtubules (and is therefore called a 9+2 axoneme). A canonical motile cilium (or eukaryotic flagellum) whose axoneme consists of nine peripheral microtubule doublets surrounding a central pair of singlet microtubules (the 9+2 arrangement). Conserved across Chlamydomonas reinhardtii, Tetrahymena thermophila, and Trypanosoma brucei, the 9+2 motile cilium integrates central pair projections, radial spokes, nexin-dynein regulatory complexes, and dynein arms to produce planar or ciliary waveforms.

A paracrystalline monomolecular array of one or more (glyco)protein species that self-assemble on the outermost surface of the cell envelope, with oblique, square or hexagonal lattice symmetry. Nonmechanistic summary of Sfi1 knockdown phenotypes (FUNCTION)
RNAi against the implicated Sfi1 isoforms	produces	Reduced myoneme cables

DOI:10.1016/j.cub.2026.06.062 PMC13637444.1 cortical-patterning Results report reduced centrin incorporation in posterior myonemes in Sfi1-1 and Sfi1-2 RNAi conditions, with altered anterior/posterior patterning rather than reduced total centrin fluorescence. Sfi1-2/Sfi1-3 cross-depletion limits isoform attribution. This remains a nonmechanistic intervention summary: cable-pattern changes and contraction impairment are parallel outcomes, not proof that cable loss mediates the defect.

DOI:10.1016/j.cub.2026.06.062 PMC13637444.1 contractile-machinery Results and STAR Methods report reduced or incomplete contraction in the implicated knockdown conditions. Sfi1-2/Sfi1-3 cross-depletion and stimulus-dependent responses preclude a universal or isoform-exclusive requirement. No exact kinetics, native force-generation mechanism or mediation by cable loss is inferred.
